intro: Outlook for property managers on Mac runs on three built-in tools: reply templates, server rules and a signature for each account. You can set all three up yourself in the new Outlook for Mac. This guide gives the menu paths, the mistakes that trip up property offices, and the moments when Lazur helps you get unstuck.
tldr: Check that you are on the new Outlook for Mac first. Microsoft says legacy Outlook stops working against Exchange Online starting October 2026.
Save your most repeated tenant replies as templates with File > Save As Template, then reuse them with File > New > Mail From Template.
Build rules under Settings > Rules. They are server rules that run top to bottom, so put the broad ones last.
Set signatures under Settings > Mail > Signatures, once for new messages and once for replies or forwards.
Lazur points at the setting, guides you one click at a time, and drafts text. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: Most of a property office runs through one inbox. Maintenance requests, rent questions, lease renewals and vendor quotes all arrive as email. Outlook for Mac can take a lot of that repetition off your plate. You do it with three tools that already exist: templates, rules and signatures. This guide walks through each one in the new app. It ends with the places where Lazur saves you time.
Check which Outlook for Mac you are running

Open Outlook and choose Outlook > About Outlook. Note the version number. Microsoft's release notes list 16.114.3 (Build 26102720) as the most recent release, dated October 27, 2026. If your build is older, choose Help > Check for Updates before you set anything up. Menus change between builds, so a path that matches your build saves you time.

The old app matters here too. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting in October 2026. It also says Exchange Web Services retires on October 1, 2026. Microsoft reports that over 95% of Microsoft 365 users have already moved to the new Outlook for Mac. That date has passed. If your mail still runs in the old app, ask your IT admin what to do before you build anything.

blocks.title: Menus moved
blocks.text: Microsoft redesigned Settings in version 16.108, released April 14, 2026. If your menus look different from the paths on this page, you are probably on an older layout. Check the build first, then follow the paths.
Build reply templates for the messages you send every week

Property managers repeat themselves. A Lobster Pack blog estimates that an 80-unit portfolio sends more than 120 communications a month. These cover maintenance requests, general inquiries, late-payment follow-ups and lease renewals. The post puts each one at 5 to 15 minutes, or 10 to 30 hours a month. It cites no source for those figures. Treat them as a rough guess, and count your own month instead.

Start with the three messages you write most. A maintenance acknowledgment, a first late-rent notice and a lease renewal reply are good picks. Replace names, unit numbers, dates and amounts with placeholders in square brackets, such as [Tenant first name] and [Unit]. Obvious placeholders are safer than blank spaces, because a blank line can look finished when it is not.

Here is a sample first notice you can adapt: 'Hi [Tenant first name], our records show that rent for [Unit] was not received by [Due date]. Please send the balance of [Amount] by [New date], or reply to this message so we can talk about a plan. Thank you, [Your name].' Check your lease and local rules before you send any notice that involves fees or deadlines.
Save a message as a template in Outlook for Mac

items: Open a new message and write the template text. Leave the To line empty.
Choose File > Save As Template.
Name it something you will recognize in a month, such as Late rent, first notice.
Optionally apply a tag, pick a location and select Save.
To use it later, choose File > New > Mail From Template, then open the .emltpl file you saved.
Add the tenant's address, fill in every placeholder, and read the message once before you send.

blocks.text: Microsoft says its built-in template controls need a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac 15.35 (170610) or later. Any current 16.x build meets that version floor. Check your build under Outlook > About Outlook if the menus look different from the steps above.
Use templates in a shared mailbox without surprises

Microsoft also describes a My Templates add-in. It works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts. It is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. If your organization has turned add-ins off, it may be missing, and Microsoft says to contact an administrator. Do not assume a shared inbox has the same templates as your own account.

A simple fix works well. Keep a master copy of each reply in a shared document or shared note. Paste in the text and fill the placeholders when a message comes in. It is slower than a template, but everyone on the team can use it. If you still need to attach the shared address, see [How to add a shared mailbox in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook).
Set up rules that sort tenant mail before you read it

Rules in the new Outlook for Mac live under Settings > Rules. Select +Add Rule. Then set a condition, an action, optional extra conditions and any exceptions. Microsoft says only server rules can be created in this version. Client rules are no longer supported.

Order matters more than most people expect. Rules run from top to bottom, in the order shown in the Rules window. The setting Stop processing more rules is on by default. So if an early rule matches a message, later rules may never see it. Put the specific rules at the top and the broad catch-all rules at the bottom.

Move to Urgent folder and flag
Sender is on your approved vendor list
blocks.caption: A sample order for a small portfolio inbox. Adjust the names to your own folders.

blocks.text: Two mistakes come up often. The first is a rule that deletes mail. Move matched messages to a folder instead, so you can recover one that matched by accident. The second is a condition that is too broad, such as the word rent anywhere in the body. It can catch your own replies too. Test with one message, then add the next rule.
Set a signature for each account and each kind of message

Signatures live under Settings > Mail > Signatures. Each mail account has its own default signature. You set For new messages and For replies or forwards independently, so one account can use a full signature on new mail and a short one on replies. To add a signature to a message you are writing, use the Signature button on the Ribbon.

A property office often sends from more than one address. Give each account a signature with the company name, the maintenance phone line and office hours. Keep it short. Tenants often read these on a phone, where a long block of text is hard to scan.

Microsoft's signature article does not say whether one account can switch between several named signatures for different properties automatically. Test that in the app before you rely on it. Until then, use a separate account per property, or insert the right signature by hand.
Newer Outlook for Mac features that help with tenant mail

items: Edit a message in the Outbox before it sends. Microsoft added this in version 16.111 on July 14, 2026.
Import PST files for emails, calendars and contacts. Added in version 16.110 on June 16, 2026, useful if you are moving old mailbox data in.
Set work hours and work-location schedules in Calendar. Added in version 16.113 on September 16, 2026.
Choose whether accepted invitations leave the Inbox. Also added in version 16.113.
Import Outlook .msg files and use the redesigned Settings. Both arrived in version 16.108 on April 14, 2026.

blocks.text: The Outbox edit suits rent notices best. Read the amount and unit number once more while the message still waits in the Outbox. Delayed sending is a related option. See [How to delay delivery of an email in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/delay-delivery-of-an-email-in-outlook) for the steps.
How much of the week goes to routine email work

A 2025 NAA and AppFolio Performance Ecosystem survey of nearly 2,000 real estate professionals found that 42% of the week goes to routine operational work. Paperwork, data entry and administrative tasks sit in that group. Another 24% goes to reactive work, such as troubleshooting. AppFolio's newsroom puts routine and reactive work together at 66%.

Read those figures with care. AppFolio sponsored the survey, and AppFolio sells property management software. The survey also covers a wider group than property managers alone. Use the numbers as a frame, not a benchmark.

The better test is your own week. Count the minutes you spend on repeat replies for one week before you set up templates. Then count the same kind of week after the templates and rules run. A count you made yourself beats any industry average.
Ask Lazur for help in Outlook, out loud

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ (Option and Command) to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

Ask where a setting is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. It does not click for you. You stay in control of Outlook, and you choose each step.

Lazur also helps with the text. Ask it to draft a reply, and it types the draft at your cursor. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Add your property names to the personal dictionary, so dictation spells them right. Snippets and clipboard slots help with the placeholders you use every week.

Here is a good first try. Open a tenant's message in Outlook for Mac, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask Lazur for a short reply about parking. Listen to the draft, then edit it in the message. Press Send yourself. Lazur does not send mail for you.
Common mistakes and edge cases

items: A template still holds a real tenant's name or amount. Check every placeholder before you save.
Expecting My Templates in a shared mailbox, where Microsoft says it is not available.
Writing a rule that deletes mail, or a condition that matches your own replies.
Forgetting that rules run top to bottom, and that Stop processing more rules is on by default.
Assuming the default signature covers replies. Check For replies or forwards separately.
Following menus from an older guide after the legacy cutover. Check your build first.

blocks.text: One edge case catches people off guard. Some organizations turn off add-ins. If your template option looks missing, that may be a policy, not a bug. Ask your administrator before you spend an afternoon on a workaround.
A setup plan you can finish in a week

items: First, check your build and install updates.
Next, save your three most repeated messages as templates.
Then, build rules for the inbox, starting with urgent maintenance.
After that, set a signature for each account and check the reply default.
Finally, log the minutes spent on email for a week, and compare.

blocks.text: Once that works, look at the rest of your inbox. The how-to pages below cover each step in more depth. Start with [How to create a rule in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook), then [How to create an email signature in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-an-email-signature-in-outlook).

Other useful pages are [How to set a reminder for an email in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/set-a-reminder-for-an-email-in-outlook) and [How to block a sender in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/block-a-sender-in-outlook). When you want to compare Lazur's plans, see the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: Is the new Outlook for Mac the version I should use?
faq.answer: Yes. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting in October 2026. Microsoft also reports that over 95% of Microsoft 365 users have moved to the new app. Check your build under Outlook > About Outlook, then run Help > Check for Updates.

faq.question: How do I save an email as a template in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Write the message, then choose File > Save As Template. Name it, optionally apply a tag, pick a location and select Save. To use it later, choose File > New > Mail From Template and open the .emltpl file. Fill every placeholder before you send.

faq.question: Why is My Templates missing in my shared mailbox?
faq.answer: Microsoft says the My Templates add-in works only with Exchange accounts. It is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. If your organization has turned add-ins off, it may be missing everywhere. Ask an administrator whether that policy applies to you.

faq.question: Can I create client rules in the new Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft says only server rules can be created in Outlook for Mac, and client rules are no longer supported. Rules run from top to bottom in the Rules window. Stop processing more rules is on by default, so put broad rules at the bottom.

faq.question: Where do I change my email signature?
faq.answer: Choose Settings > Mail > Signatures. Each mail account has its own default. Set For new messages and For replies or forwards separately. While you compose, use the Signature button on the Ribbon to insert one.

faq.question: Can Lazur send tenant emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text, and it guides you through steps. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. You read the message and press Send yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my screen all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut, ⌥ ⌘. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.
